correctness.rationale: For every nonnegative diagonal length t in E, the two endpoints yield a lower point and an upper point enclosing an axis-aligned box of shortest side at least t; the converse holds by taking the lower corner. This proves the finite pairwise max-min identity independently. Dominated points can be replaced by coordinatewise stronger points. Along sorted planar Pareto fronts the two gaps are oppositely strictly monotone, making each upper-index score unimodal with maximum at the immediate crossing predecessor or successor. Crossing thresholds are nondecreasing along the lower front, yielding at most |U*| pointer advances and 2|L*| score evaluations. Exact integer and rational comparisons reproduced the all-pairs result in 114,400 cases, including empty/zero-width and tie scenarios. These tests are corroboration only; the theorem is proved analytically.

value.rationale: The original width is a genuine repeatedly evaluated stopping-quality measure in biobjective enclosing-set optimization, not a contrived scalar invariant. On already sorted antichains, checking \(|L_*|\,|U_*|\) boxes is replaced by a sharp at-most-two-upper-candidates-per-lower-point structural certificate computed via \(|L_*|+|U_*|\) work, returning an auditable maximizing witness and handling empty enclosures. Arbitrary input inherits an \(O(N\log N)\) algorithm. This is potentially valuable precisely for large finite fronts and repeated width checks, with no unproved solver-wide runtime gain asserted.
